parts.label: Understand
parts.title: Use the AI RMF as a decision loop
parts.body:
The NIST AI Risk Management Framework gives an organization four functions: GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE, and MANAGE. GOVERN sets responsibility, policy, risk tolerance, and oversight across the lifecycle. MAP establishes the system's purpose, setting, people affected, dependencies, and plausible harms. MEASURE tests those risks with methods that resemble actual use. MANAGE decides how to respond, then monitors what happens. The functions are connected and iterative; NIST says they are not an ordered checklist.

For an executive, the loop has three decision points. Before funding, ask whether the purpose and potential impact justify exploration. Before release, ask whether testing supports the proposed scope and whether remaining risk has an owner with authority to accept it. In operation, ask whether changed data, model behavior, users, or suppliers make the earlier decision stale. An inventory entry should name those decisions and their evidence.

The RMF is voluntary guidance. It does not certify a product, supply legal permission, or set universal error thresholds. Counsel must map actual deployment to applicable law. The organization sets tolerance appropriate to the stakes: a missed meeting-summary detail and a mistaken employment decision should not share a release test.

example.title: A hiring pilot changes the question
example.body: A recruitment assistant initially summarizes job descriptions. The team later proposes ranking applicants. That change triggers a new MAP review because candidates and decisions are affected differently. The launch packet now needs comparison with existing screening, subgroup analysis where lawful and feasible, reviewer instructions, and a route for disputed outcomes.

exercise.title: Write the four-function record
exercise.body: Choose one AI use. In four rows, list the owner and artifact for GOVERN, affected groups and failure modes for MAP, a test and deployment-like dataset for MEASURE, and a release condition plus monitoring trigger for MANAGE. Identify the decision blocked by each missing artifact.

parts.label: Map
parts.title: Define risk in the setting where the system will work
parts.body:
A model score has little meaning without a task and setting. MAP asks who will use the output, who may be affected, what the existing workflow does, and what the system can influence. Record intended purpose, excluded uses, data and supplier dependencies, potential benefits, and harms. Include process workers and people subject to its decisions. They often see failure modes the development team misses.

For a hiring assistant, distinguish drafting a recruiter note from excluding applicants. Trace the path from applicant data to recommendation to human decision. Can a reviewer inspect evidence, override the suggestion, and explain the outcome? Consider language, accessibility, and differences across offices. Paris may bring the EU AI Act and GDPR into scope; Toronto requires separate Canadian privacy and employment review. The RMF supplies a risk method; counsel identifies obligations.

End MAP with a go, narrow, or stop decision. If representative evaluation data cannot be lawfully obtained, reduce the use case. If a vendor cannot explain data handling or logging, record that uncertainty. A register listing only 'bias' and 'hallucination' without a pathway to harm cannot guide release.

example.title: A usable risk statement
example.body: If summaries omit experience from nonstandard résumés, recruiters may overlook qualified applicants. Compare the tool and existing process on representative application types. The hiring executive owns the outcome, with privacy and employment-law review.

exercise.title: Map a pathway to harm
exercise.body: Draw five boxes for data, model, output, human action, and affected person. Trace one failure through them, name who could notice it, and identify missing evidence. Decide whether to fund a test, narrow scope, or decline the use case.

parts.label: Measure
parts.title: Demand evidence that matches the decision
parts.body:
MEASURE turns a risk statement into a test. Choose a baseline, cases from the proposed operating setting, grading method, acceptable range, and owner before seeing results. Include ordinary and difficult cases. For generative systems, test unsupported claims, sensitive-data disclosure, and attacks through untrusted text when relevant. One aggregate score can hide severe failures in a small category.

A release packet should show sample selection, results by relevant slice, uncertainty or limitations, error severity, and comparison with the current process. Test human review as a control: can reviewers detect an error under realistic workload, and can they change the outcome? Independent review can expose blind spots. Document risks you cannot measure reliably rather than treating the missing metric as assurance.

Set a use-specific threshold. A meeting-note assistant may allow correction before distribution; an unreviewed adverse recruitment decision may be outside risk tolerance. These illustrate the reasoning and are not NIST prescribed numbers.

example.title: A test changes the launch plan
example.body: In a hypothetical test of 200 historical applications, 12 summaries omit a required qualification. Recruiters detect half under usual review time. Keep the tool in draft-assist mode, improve source display, and rerun a blinded review test before ranking use. These figures are illustrative.

exercise.title: Make one risk measurable
exercise.body: Write a one-page test plan for a consequential error. Specify baseline, sampling, slices, severity scale, reviewer task, threshold, and response to a missed threshold. Explain what evidence would change your release recommendation.

parts.label: Manage
parts.title: Set a release boundary and revisit it
parts.body:
MANAGE is where an executive accepts a bounded risk or refuses it. Record permitted users, data, tasks, geography, autonomy, controls, and review date. If the team changes the model, prompt, connector, population, or downstream authority, decide which tests run again. Assign someone able to pause use when a trigger is met. Saying that humans remain responsible does not tell an operator when to intervene.

A monthly operational review can inspect errors, overrides, complaints, changing inputs, near misses, and supplier changes. Severity matters more than incident count. Define escalation times and decision authority for material harm, a privacy event, or a failed control. Retirement requires revoking credentials, stopping scheduled runs, retaining required records, and checking that outputs no longer drive decisions.

Give executives the benefit against baseline, residual risks, gaps, mitigation cost, owner, and requested choice: expand, continue a limited pilot, remediate, or stop. The RMF makes the choice traceable; the accountable executive makes it.

example.title: A bounded approval
example.body: Approve an internal claims-drafting assistant for trained adjusters in one region for eight weeks. It cannot send a decision to a customer. Weekly sampling must stay within a locally defined severe-error limit. Two severe cases in a week trigger a pause and review. This threshold is illustrative, not a NIST requirement.

exercise.title: Draft a reversible decision
exercise.body: Write a six-line approval: scope, evidence, residual risk, accountable executive, monitoring trigger, and rollback step. Name one change that invalidates approval and the test required before expansion.

sources: NIST AI RMF Core: MANAGE and GOVERN
